title: MQTT TLS trust manager only checks that the certificate subject contains "keenon"/"keenoon"
evidence: Disassembly of DynamicMqttServer$2.checkTrusted: for each cert getSubjectDN().toString().toLowerCase() must contain "keenon" or "keenoon" else CertificateException; no signature/chain/expiry/hostname validation. buildSSLSocketFactory passes this TrustManager (mLocalTrustManger) only when Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 29, otherwise null (default handling of the BKS trust store). The trust BKS files in res/raw contain private CA entries.
impact: Man-in-the-middle of the cloud command channel; forged remote commands (WF-8).
remediation: Pin the broker CA (or leaf) properly using the default PKIX validation with the embedded CA, plus hostname verification.
description: On Android 10+ images an attacker able to intercept the MQTT TLS connection (e.g. via DNS/ARP spoofing on the robot Wi-Fi) can present a self-signed certificate whose subject contains "keenon" and be accepted, gaining the ability to read/inject robot commands and telemetry. Practical exploitability also depends on the broker requiring the fleet client certificate (see PCL-052 shared client keystore) and on the OS version of the robot tablet (UNKNOWN).
reproduction: python -I scripts/pcl/dis.py <base> 'Lcom/keenon/component/core/mqtt/DynamicMqttServer$2;' checkTrusted

title: Weak/misused cryptography in registration, domain cache and utilities
evidence: JADX AesUtil.getSecretKey: KeyGenerator AES-128 seeded from SecureRandom("SHA1PRNG").setSeed(password) (non-portable deterministic KDF); cipher AES/CTR/NoPadding (no integrity, IV reuse risk) ; key/IV for registration (aes_register_key/iv) and aes_dev_key/iv are static fleet-wide values from libcipher_pack; AesUtil.generateKeyOrIV builds random strings with Math.random(); RegisterDeviceHelper nonce uses java.util.Random; DesUtil (DES) and MD5/SHA1 helpers exist; encrypted domain config file is decrypted and the plaintext is logged (CoreLog "decryptDomainData:: result=").
impact: Tamperable local domain/region cache (could redirect the robot to another cloud host if the cache file is writable); weak key derivation.
remediation: Use AES-GCM with random IV, PBKDF2/Argon2 or Keystore keys; SecureRandom; remove DES/MD5 for security uses; do not log decrypted data.
description: Constant key/IV with CTR mode means the encrypted SN/domain payloads are malleable and, if IV is reused with different plaintexts, keystream-reuse applies. Impact is bounded by what the data protects (SN, region domain selection).
reproduction: REA/JADX: rea.sh inspect-android-method <apk> com.keenon.module.datasync.utils.AesUtil getSecretKey (decompiled body saved under pcl_out/jadx/); REA/JADX: rea.sh inspect-android-method <apk> com.keenon.component.core.config.domain.DomainManager decryptDomainData (decompiled body saved under pcl_out/jadx/)
